question: Is the Aurzen TravelPlay a good back seat screen for a Tesla Model Y? Where can I buy one?
query: Aurzen TravelPlay review Tesla Model Y compatibility where to buy

replays.text:
**It could be a good back-seat viewing setup if you want a large projection surface for parked-car movie nights—but it’s not an electronic screen or projector.** The TravelPlay is a foldable screen/sunshade, so you’ll also need a compatible portable projector. Aurzen lists roughly 47- and 50-inch panels, tool-free clip-in installation, and rear-seat, tailgate, and sky-roof modes. [Product details](https://aurzen.com/collections/new-releases/products/aurzen-travelplay-autocinema-screen-for-tesla-model-y)

**Fit matters:** it’s designed for the refreshed 2025–2026 Model Y. Aurzen says it can work with 2020–2024 models in sky-roof mode, but the rear screen won’t fully cover the window. And projection is for use **only while parked**.

You can buy it directly from [Aurzen](https://aurzen.com/collections/new-releases/products/aurzen-travelplay-autocinema-screen-for-tesla-model-y). The listing shows **$119.99** and says it’s available in the U.S. only. I’d consider it if you already own a portable projector; otherwise, factor in the cost and hassle of one.

**It can be a good rear-seat viewing screen if you want a projector setup—not a standalone video screen.** TravelPlay is a foldable screen and sunshade; you’ll need a compatible portable projector, which isn’t listed among the included items. It offers a rear-seat mode, tool-free clip installation, and two panels measuring about 47″ and 50″. Use it **only while the Tesla is parked**. ([Aurzen product page](https://aurzen.com/collections/new-releases/products/aurzen-travelplay-autocinema-screen-for-tesla-model-y))
